Use tables for data organized in rows and columns. To place links or content
side by side, use cards and grids instead.
All the table types below are built-in; the Doctools CSS classes at the end
are optional.

Prefer list-table for hand-maintained data. Each
outer item is a row; each inner item is a cell. Every row must contain the same
number of cells. `header-rows` identifies column headers, `stub-columns`
identifies row headers, and `widths` sets relative column widths:

```rst

Use csv-table for imported or generated data.
`file` is relative to the source document; `header-rows: 1` uses the file’s
first row as headings:

```rst

   :widths: 25 75
```

Doctools custom Sphinx directives allow better formatting, and add extra

Below, every added directive is explained with examples. For built-in code

To allow arranging content in a tabular manner while still respecting multiple
screen sizes for both HTML and PDF output, two container directives are available:
`flex` and `grid`.

The flex directive implements a subset of
CSS Flex.
It is used to arrange elements without worrying about number of columns and sizes,
while still obtaining a fairly good result.

```rst
.. flex::
   :class: [badges, ...]
```

The grid directive implements a subset of
CSS Grids.
It is used to arrange elements with exact number of columns and width control.

```rst
.. grid::
   :columns: 3
```

A card directive is meant to be used inside a Grid or
Flex. It creates a card element and allows to link to a
reference. Only references are allowed by design, to discourage arbitrary
linking.

```rst

   :ref: <ref>
```
